tactic: Hard-to-cancel subscriptions, retention flows, unannounced renewals
consumer_harm: Inertia and friction keep people paying for unwanted subscriptions; tested retention questions can move choices against consumers' values
us_law: ROSCA 15 USC 8401-8405; FTC Act s5; FTC negative option ANPRM (13 Mar 2026)
status_2026_11: 2024 click-to-cancel rule vacated 8 Jul 2025; new ANPRM pending; ROSCA in force
illinois: 815 ILCS 601 (online cancellation for online sign-ups since 2022)
international: CA Bus & Prof 17602 (AB 2863); MN 325G.58; EU Digital Fairness Act (proposal due Nov 2026)
enforcement_examples: FTC v. Amazon (Prime) $2.5B, Sep 2025; FTC + 21 states v. Uber (Uber One), pending
discussion_question: A retention flow lifts 12-month renewals 8 points in an A/B test. What must you measure before calling it a success?

tactic: Drip pricing, junk fees, hidden mandatory fees
consumer_harm: Shrouded fees raise spending and purchase probability and impede comparison
us_law: FTC Act s5; 16 CFR 464 (tickets, short-term lodging, eff. 12 May 2025)
status_2026_11: Fees rule in force for tickets and lodging; s5 elsewhere
international: UK DMCC Act (CMA fines: AA/BSM, StubHub); EU UCPD
enforcement_examples: FTC + Illinois AG v. Grubhub $140M judgment ($25M paid), Dec 2024; FTC v. Live Nation/Ticketmaster, pending (C.D. Cal.)
discussion_question: Your conjoint shows lower sensitivity to a 'service fee' than to base price. Is using that legal in your industry? Ethical?

tactic: Fake, bought, sentiment-conditioned or suppressed reviews; fake followers; AI-written reviews
consumer_harm: Corrupts the main online quality signal and shifts demand to worse products
us_law: 16 CFR 465 (eff. 21 Oct 2024; civil penalties); FTC Act s5
status_2026_11: In force; warning letters to 10 companies
evidence: Fashion Nova $4.2M (2022, review suppression); Rytr (2024, AI testimonials)
column12: Your fake-review detector could also generate undetectable fakes. What does Part 465's 'should have known' standard imply?

tactic: Undisclosed influencer, employee or native advertising
consumer_harm: Consumers treat paid promotion as independent recommendation
us_law: Endorsement Guides 16 CFR 255 (2023); FTC Act s5
international: EU UCPD (disguised advertising); EU Digital Fairness Act (proposal)
enforcement_examples: FTC warning letters to brands and influencers
discussion_question: Undisclosed posts drive 40% more clicks. What, if anything, should you do with that estimate?

tactic: Fake countdowns and scarcity, nagging after refusals, confirmshaming
consumer_harm: Rushes or wears down decisions; consumers forgo worthwhile review
us_law: FTC Act s5 (false claims); FTC dark patterns staff report (2022)
international: EU UCPD Annex I point 7; DSA deceptive design (X EUR120M, Dec 2025)
enforcement_examples: Epic Games (Fortnite) $245M refunds + $275M COPPA penalty, Dec 2022
discussion_question: Design an experiment that separates 'the timer made people decide faster' from 'the timer made people decide worse'.

tactic: Personalised prices from personal data; shared pricing algorithms
consumer_harm: Price discrimination using data consumers did not knowingly trade; algorithmic coordination
status_2026_11: FTC 6(b) study (Jan 2025 findings); DOJ-RealPage proposed settlement (24 Nov 2025)
international: NY GBL 349-a disclosure (in force Nov 2025); bans: MD HB 895 (in force 1 Oct 2026), CT PA 26-130 (eff. 1 Jul 2027), NJ A4085 (eff. 1 Aug 2027); NY One Fair Price Act passed Jun 2026, not yet delivered to Governor; NY 349-a appeal argued 19 Oct 2026
evidence: Dube-Misra 2023; Calvano et al. 2020; Assad et al. 2024
discussion_question: Your model predicts willingness to pay from zip code and device. Which uses need a NY disclosure, which are banned in CT, and which exemptions would you rely on?

tactic: Pre-ticked consent, asymmetric opt-outs, over-collection, biometric capture, scraping against terms
consumer_harm: Loss of control over personal data; costs hidden from consumers
us_law: COPPA 16 CFR 312 (amended; compliance 22 Apr 2026); FTC Act s5
illinois: BIPA 740 ILCS 14 ($1,000/$5,000 per violation; private right of action)
international: CCPA regs 11 CCR 7004 (symmetry); GDPR; EU AI Act
enforcement_examples: CPPA v. Honda $632,500 (Mar 2025); Todd Snyder $345,178 (May 2025); FTC v. Rite Aid facial recognition ban (Dec 2023)
evidence: Acquisti-Taylor-Wagman 2016; Nouwens et al. 2020; Johnson-Shriver-Goldberg 2023; Aridor-Che-Salz 2023
discussion_question: Which customer data may you paste into an AI assistant, and under which university policy?

tactic: Loot boxes, virtual currencies, ads targeted at minors
consumer_harm: Obscured real prices and exploitation of limited self-control
international: EU AI Act Art. 5 (exploiting age vulnerabilities); EU DFA (proposal)
enforcement_examples: HoYoverse (Genshin Impact) $20M, Jan 2025; Epic Games, Dec 2022
discussion_question: Should a game's A/B test of loot-box odds displays be allowed for under-16 players at all?

tactic: Unsubstantiated AI capability claims ('AI washing'); AI tools sold for deception
consumer_harm: Buyers pay for capabilities that do not exist; AI scales deceptive content
enforcement_examples: DoNotPay, Rytr (2024); Workado (2025); Air AI (2025, pending); Cox Media Group 'Active Listening' $930K (Aug 2026)
discussion_question: Your model has 71% hold-out accuracy. What may you claim in a pitch deck?

tactic: Ad delivery and targeting that skews by protected traits
consumer_harm: Exclusion from housing, credit or job opportunities
us_law: Fair Housing Act; ECOA; Title VII
enforcement_examples: U.S. v. Meta Platforms (housing ads), settled Jun 2022
discussion_question: Your lookalike audience is cheaper but skews male. When does cost optimisation become a legal problem?

consumer_harm: Consumers pay premiums for unverified benefits
us_law: Green Guides 16 CFR 260; FTC Act s5
evidence: Rao-Wang 2017 (false health claims and FTC action)
discussion_question: Classify a sample of product-page claims as specific, generic or unverifiable.

tactic: A/B tests that include deceptive variants; 'ship the winner' with opposed interests
consumer_harm: Testing a deceptive arm deceives everyone in it; selection finds the most harmful variant
us_law: FTC Act s5 applies to each tested variant
discussion_question: Your retention test's winning arm raised renewals. Show that it did not do so by moving choices against customers' interests.
